# THE FAILURE STORY

It's late July. The team has 43 commits across 10 worktrees, with the primary branch sitting on claimgate/bypass-regression—meant to be the integration point. During testing and debugging from July 15-18, someone made 180 local edits: test data files, config tweaks, logging patches, one-off boundary checks. Nobody committed these. When merge day arrives, the first attempt hits git's safety wall: "Your local changes to system_v5/handler.py would be overwritten by merge." The team stashes the dirty state and tries again. But now they discover the 43 commits have hidden cross-dependencies. A commit in worktree-3 rewrites a schema that worktree-7's commit also modifies; both expect different incoming state. Merge aborts with a conflict. They stash again. By now the dirty files are gone from working tree but still in the reflog, and nobody can reconstruct which stash belongs to which branch.
